brief: Compare highest-rate-first and smallest-balance-first repayment using the same feasible surplus.

en-US.scenario: Fictional US-dollar examples for "Compare repayment orders"; illustrative amounts, not current prices or product offers. No assumption of salary, bank ownership or spare income.

es-MX.scenario: Ejemplos ficticios en pesos mexicanos para "Compara órdenes de pago"; montos ilustrativos, no precios vigentes ni ofertas. No se supone nómina, cuenta bancaria ni dinero sobrante.

pt-BR.scenario: Exemplos fictícios em reais para "Compare ordens de pagamento"; valores ilustrativos, não preços atuais nem ofertas. Sem supor salário, conta bancária ou dinheiro sobrando.

objective.observable_action: Compare highest-rate-first and smallest-balance-first repayment using the same feasible surplus.
objective.success_criterion: Complete the fresh-context transfer using only its visible information.

instruction.relevance: After essentials and required payments, compare what the same feasible extra payment changes.
instruction.misconception: Confusing highest-rate-first with smallest-balance-first, or comparing them using different available surpluses.
instruction.numeracy_support: Every quantity and assumption needed to decide is visible in the current scenario. Examples explain the relationship before independent application.

evidence.reasoning: Highest-rate-first targets cost; smallest-balance-first targets an earlier account closure. Compare both using the same feasible extra payment and actual terms.
Same extra principal payment; different modeled interest costs avoided.
This method orders by remaining balance, not interest rate.
250 − 100 = 150 remains; this debt is not closed yet.
Different funding assumptions do not isolate the effect of repayment order.
With the same extra 50, highest-rate-first selects A; smallest-balance-first selects B.

delayed_retrieval.fresh_context: Retrieve this competence in the declared later course reviews and through the existing shared review system.
